title: 2023年12月四级真题 第3套 阅读2
paperTitle: 2023年12月大学英语四级真题（第3套）
passage:
P1 People in business often make decisions based on their own personal feelings or instincts. It is quite horrifying to see people being guided by some unknown force. But how wise is it, really, to let your instincts drive your decisions?

P2 In the decision-making process, relying on instincts only makes sense when you have a vast experience to support you. Simply "feeling" that something is right or should be done is highly subjective and can drown you.

P3 On the other hand, there is a more rational approach to making decisions. Data and analysis have long been associated with informed decisions. These reduce the likelihood of errors and increase the chances of success. Big, systematic data is mostly the foundation of most of our decisions, personal and business alike. But with its extreme usability comes a complication: what do you do if you strongly feel something should not be done, even if the data insists that it should?

P4 This seemingly easy question is what drives the need to understand the relationship between instincts and data in the decision-making process. Without making things complicated, the solution to this dilemma is using data and instincts in conjunction to arrive at the best possible decisions.

P5 Instinctive decisions are always backed by previous experiences or information, which acknowledges that instinctive decisions have worked in the past. Decisions are not about making the choice and braving the consequences because you want to blindly trust your instincts. They are about combining your inner wisdom with the knowledge of systematic data to make the best decisions.

P6 Sometimes, rational analysis and data are impractical to be employed in certain situations. Absence of definitive criteria, and time and resource constraints, and novel situations are instances which limit the practicality of data. The only feasible option is to rely on what your instincts tell you. In these situations, instincts can help you make effective and quick decisions.

P7 Combining instinctive and rational analysis produces well-rounded decisions. It reduces the chances of making mistakes, and has increasingly become a favorite approach to decision-making among leaders of today.

questions.q: What does the author say businesspeople often do?
options: Strive to make sense of some unknown forces.
Avoid being driven by their own feeling.
Draw on a vast wealth of past experience.
questions.explain:
【判型】What does the author say businesspeople often do? 问的是「商人通常做什么」这一可 在原文逐字核实的客观行为，不含 infer/imply。

【拆句】题干主干是 What does the author say businesspeople often do?，what 作宾语前置； the author say 是插入成分，可剥离；剥离后等价于「Businesspeople often do what?」 结构平铺，无陷阱。

【定位】People in business often make decisions based on their own personal feelings or instincts. 商界人士常常基于自己的个人感觉或直觉做决策。

【选项】A) 无中生有 原文用 unknown force 比喻直觉的神秘性，并未让商人「弄清未知力量」；Strive to make sense of some unknown forces 凭空给出动作。 B) 与原文相反 原文说商人「常凭感觉决策」，Avoid being driven by their own feeling 却说「避免 被感觉驱动」，完全反向。 C) 张冠李戴 relying on instincts only makes sense when you have a vast experience to support you 是作者给「合理使用直觉」开的条件，并非商人「实际正在做的事」。 D) ✓ 正确 make decisions based on their own personal feelings or instincts ↔ Rely on instincts in decision-making 预判「依赖直觉作决策」与 Rely on instincts in decision-making 高度重合，正确项 锁定。 为了做出明智的决策,我们应该考虑什么? A) 出错的可能性。 B) 系统性的数据和分析。 C) 情况的复杂性。 D) 个人感受和商业策略。

questions.q: What should we take into account in order to make informed decisions?
questions.explain:
【判型】What should we take into account in order to make informed decisions? 问的是「为 了做出明智决策应当考虑什么」，答案是原文直接陈述的因素。

【拆句】题干主干 What should we take into account，what 作 take into account 的宾语前置； in order to make informed decisions 是表目的的不定式状语；句式简单。

【定位】Data and analysis have long been associated with informed decisions. 数据与分析长期以来一直与明智的决策紧密相关。 52. What should we take into account in order to make informed decisions? A) The likelihood of errors. B) Systematic data and analysis. C) The complexity of circumstances. D) Personal feelings and business strategies

【选项】A) 答非所问 原文 These reduce the likelihood of errors 说数据与分析「降低出错概率」，The likelihood of errors 只是数据带来的「结果」，不是「应当考虑的因素」。 B) ✓ 正确 Data and analysis ↔Systematic data and analysis 预判「依靠数据与分析」与 Systematic data and analysis 完全对应，且原文 Big, systematic data 进一步加固，正确项锁定。 C) 无中生有 原文从未出现 The complexity of circumstances（环境的复杂性）这一表述，与「明 智决策的依靠」无关。 D) 偷换概念 原文把 personal feelings or instincts 视作「常被依赖却需谨慎」的对象，并未把它与 business strategies 并列为「做明智决策的因素」。 在决策过程中,如果直觉与数据不一致,人们应该怎么做? A) 用以往的经验解决这个两难困境。 B) 弄清楚两者中哪一个更可靠。 C) 将两者结合起来。 D) 让直觉优先于数据。

questions.q: What should people do in a decision-making process if instincts disagree with data?
options: Resolve the dilemma with previous experience.
Figure out which of the two is more reliable.
questions.explain:
【判型】What should people do in a decision-making process if instincts disagree with data? 问的是作者给出的具体做法，原文有 using data and instincts in conjunction 直陈方案。

【拆句】题干 What should people do in a decision-making process if instincts disagree with data? 主句是 What should people do，in a decision-making process 介词短语作地点 状语；if instincts disagree with data 是 if 引导的条件状语从句；结构清楚。

【定位】Without making things complicated, the solution to this dilemma is using data and instincts in conjunction to arrive at the best possible decisions. 简单来说，这一难题的解决方案是把数据和直觉结合起来使用，以达成最佳的决策。 53. What should people do in a decision-making process if instincts disagree with data? A) Resolve the dilemma with previous experience. B) Figure out which of the two is more reliable. C) Combine the two together. D) Prioritize instincts over data.

【选项】A) 张冠李戴 Instinctive decisions are always backed by previous experiences 是「直觉的支撑机 制」，不是题干问的「矛盾时的解决办法」。 B) 无中生有 原文从未让人「比较谁更可靠」，Figure out which of the two is more reliable 是凭 空增加的取舍动作。 C) ✓ 正确 using data and instincts in conjunction ↔Combine the two together 预判「把数据与直觉结合使用」与 Combine the two together 完全等价，正确项 锁定。 D) 与原文相反 原文明确反对盲目信任直觉（you want to blindly trust your instincts 被作者否定）， Prioritize instincts over data 却把直觉摆在数据之上，反向。 当面对限制数据实用性的各种因素时,我们应该怎么做? A) 进行理性和系统的分析。 B) 探索最可行的选择。 C) 求助于我们内在的智慧。 D) 应用明确的标准。

questions.q: What should we do when facing various factors that limit the practicality of data?
options: Make a rational and systematic analysis.
questions.explain:
【判型】What should we do when facing various factors that limit the practicality of data? 问 的是特定情境下的做法，仍是定位＋复述。

【拆句】题干主句 What should we do，when facing various factors 是 when 引导的现在分词时 间状语，省略主语 we；that limit the practicality of data 是定语从句，修饰 factors。基 础薄弱的同学要看清「factors」才是从句修饰对象，而不是「we」。

【定位】The only feasible option is to rely on what your instincts tell you. 唯一可行的办法，是依靠你的直觉告诉你的东西。 54. What should we do when facing various factors that limit the practicality of data? A) Make a rational and systematic analysis. B) Explore the most feasible options. C) Resort to our inner wisdom. D) Apply definitive criteria.

【选项】A) 与原文相反 原文明说数据在此场合「不可行」，Make a rational and systematic analysis 反让你 做理性系统分析，正好走反方向。 B) 偷换概念 原文说 The only feasible option is to rely on what your instincts tell you，给出的 是「唯一可行的办法」；Explore the most feasible options 把「唯一选项」偷换成 「探索多个最可行选项」，且把动作偷换成「探索」。 C) ✓ 正确 rely on what your instincts tell you ↔Resort to our inner wisdom 预判「依靠直觉」与 Resort to our inner wisdom（求助内在智慧）通过 P5 给出的等 价关系完全对应，正确项锁定。 D) 与原文相反 原文 Absence of definitive criteria 指出此场合「没有明确标准」，Apply definitive criteria 反让你「应用明确标准」，与原文完全对立。 根据作者的观点,决策要成为最佳决策需要什么? A) 结合运用直觉和数据。 B) 在做出选择时评估所有因素。 C) 回忆过去实际奏效的做法。 D) 避免随意相信直觉。

questions.q: What does it take for decisions to become the best according to the author?
options: Applying instincts and data in conjunction.
Assessing all factors when making a choice.
Recalling what has actually worked in the past.
questions.explain:
【判型】What does it take for decisions to become the best according to the author? 问的是 「让决策成为最佳」的所需条件，是原文有明确句子可对应的细节，并非要从全文归纳的 主旨。

【拆句】题干 What does it take for decisions to become the best according to the author? 句 型为「it takes sth for sb/sth to do sth」，what 替换 sth 提前；for decisions 是 take 的逻辑主语；to become the best 是真正的目的不定式。看懂这个句型是关键，否则容易 把题干误读成主旨题。

【定位】Combining instinctive and rational analysis produces well-rounded decisions. 把直觉与理性分析结合起来，能产出周全的决策。 55. What does it take for decisions to become the best according to the author? A) Applying instincts and data in conjunction. B) Assessing all factors when making a choice. C) Recalling what has actually worked in the past. D) Refraining from trusting instincts arbitrarily.

【选项】A) ✓ 正确 Combining instinctive and rational analysis ↔Applying instincts and data in conjunction using data and instincts in conjunction to arrive at the best possible decisions ↔ Applying instincts and data in conjunction 预判「直觉＋理性分析联用」与 Applying instincts and data in conjunction 完全对 应，且 P4 与 P7 双句佐证，正确项锁定。 B) 无中生有 原文从未要求「评估所有因素」，Assessing all factors when making a choice 是无 来源的扩张表述。 C) 以偏概全 Instinctive decisions are always backed by previous experiences 只是说直觉以经验 为后盾，并不等于「让决策变最佳」的充分条件，Recalling what has actually worked in the past 把直觉一侧的支撑当成全部条件。 D) 以偏概全 you want to blindly trust your instincts 提到「不要盲目相信直觉」，但这只是「最佳 决策」的一个否定性前提，不是充分条件，Refraining from trusting instincts arbitrarily 把单一前提当成全部条件。
